userAuthorization: User instructed root to implement scheduling using the spec pipeline. Prior planning defaults are the working implementation scope unless the user steers them; not represented as separately approved policy answers.

functional.description: Support at most one recurring operational schedule per individual saved Studio test using its registered CSI and persisted environment/configuration, without creating a catalog check.
functional.rationale: Individual-test MVP bounds the requested scheduling enhancement.

functional.description: Expose typed schedule create/read/update/pause/resume/remove operations through the Studio API, with CSI read/write authorization, nondisclosing resource denial and optimistic schedule-version conflicts. Create paused by default.
functional.rationale: Existing check schedule CRUD cannot target a Studio test ID.

functional.description: Normalize five-field cron to six fields with zero seconds for minute granularity; persist an explicit valid IANA timezone or UTC default. Server preview and due selection share one recurrence resolver and return absolute UTC/local/offset times.
functional.rationale: Existing dialog relative estimates do not establish actual due time.

functional.description: Every due occurrence reuses Studio readiness, deletion/quarantine, reference, runtime, authorization and global/per-CSI pending-quota checks. Never compile or confirm from scheduled work; record COMPILE_REQUIRED before acceptance when readiness requires it.
functional.rationale: Inherited Studio scheduling and trust requirements.

functional.description: Activate or explicitly Resume against the exact current confirmed executable revision. Execution-affecting edits durably require Resume after preparation/confirmation; confirmation alone does not resume. Preserve author enabled/paused intent and already accepted immutable inputs.
functional.rationale: Unattended changes require explicit renewed activation intent.

functional.description: Give each nominal due occurrence durable identity and decision. Deduplicate concurrent polling/restarts/replicas, persist occurrence disposition plus accepted execution/ledger and schedule advancement atomically, and independently suppress duplicate repeated local-clock slots across schedule edits/activation/removal recreation.
functional.rationale: Prevent duplicate browser effects or lost accepted work.

functional.description: Persist and expose bounded paginated occurrence outcomes ACCEPTED, REFUSED, SKIPPED or DEFERRED with due time, stable reason and optional actual execution link. A refusal creates no synthetic browser run or video.
functional.rationale: COMPILE_REQUIRED and other unaccepted outcomes must remain visible.

functional.description: Skip historical catch-up, consider at most the latest eligible due slot inside configurable grace, and defer the same not-yet-accepted occurrence on capacity/temporary outage until grace expiry. Record skipped-range/expired decisions without unbounded slot enumeration. Lifecycle interruption atomically settles any outstanding DEFERRED occurrence before pause, schedule configuration update, removal or input/revision/lifecycle invalidation supersedes its cursor, preserving immutable identity/audit and preventing orphan deferred history. While scheduling capability is off, persisted deferred work remains inspectable as suspended/expired; on reenable process that identity first, settle expired as GRACE_EXPIRED without send and advance future-only, or accept the same identity once if still within grace and all gates pass.
functional.rationale: Avoid historical browser-effect replay and unbounded backlog.

functional.description: Pause/removal stop future schedule acceptance after commit and retain audit. They do not cancel already accepted runs; explicit existing run cancellation remains separate. Test deletion/quarantine preserves existing pre-send lifecycle denial. Global Studio execution disable stops new scheduled acceptance independently.
functional.rationale: Pause intent must serialize with durable acceptance while preserving existing lifecycle behavior.

functional.description: Add immutable scheduled trigger, schedule/occurrence/version/activation and nominal due provenance to existing Studio run history/details, linking actual accepted executions and protected evidence. Distinguish due, acceptance and browser-start times; legacy attribution stays Unknown. Every successful activation/Resume creates an immutable human activator/time event linked to occurrences, including clean activations with no uncertainty; subsequent edit, Resume or removal/recreation never rewrites prior actor/principal/environment/revision provenance.
functional.rationale: Scheduling evidence reuses existing Studio history without inventing results.

functional.description: Use an approved CSI/environment background service principal or platform-approved renewable delegation with a separately recorded human activator. Verify current execution/secret grants at activation, acceptance and pre-send; missing/unwired/revoked authorization fails closed. Never retain login JWTs or secret values. Server-derived activation actor/time is recorded for every successful Resume in an immutable activation event, independently of uncertainty acknowledgment rows.
functional.rationale: Current authenticated manual-user permission is not an unattended production grant.

functional.description: Operate and verify schedule management, recurrence, due acceptance, health and outcomes through API/terminal clients without requiring the frontend. Extend saved-test editor and Tests menu using centralized client, typed contracts and MSW-backed schedule scenarios.
functional.rationale: Repository mock-first delivery and AIOX CLI-first operation.

functional.description: Skip scheduled acceptance while any run for the same test has a non-DONE ledger state, including manual, finalizing and ambiguous attempts. Check under the test lock without locking existing ledger rows. Do not implicitly narrow or serialize manual execution policy.
functional.rationale: Bound unattended overlap without callback lock inversion.

functional.description: After a relevant manual or scheduled run closes with DISPATCH_UNKNOWN, START_TIMEOUT or STALE, durably block recurrence until operator investigation and explicitly audited authorized Resume acknowledges uncertainty. Resume schedules future slots only; never automatically replay an ambiguous attempt.
functional.rationale: A terminal ledger state does not establish known browser side effects.

functional.description: Skip nonexistent spring-forward slots and execute once per matching repeated fallback local-clock slot using its earlier offset. Apply the same policy to preview, dispatch and schedule-version changes.
functional.rationale: Actual Spring runtime returns both offsets; once-per-slot suppression must be explicit.

functional.description: Provide schedule status/next due/reason surfaces, authoritative preview, separate pause/removal, explicit Resume and retained values on errors/conflicts. Dirty authoring drafts cannot ambiguously create or enable a saved schedule. Scheduling never implicitly saves, compiles or confirms draft changes.
functional.rationale: Preserve the Studio review trust model and understandable operator actions.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given an authorized reader/writer and a saved confirmed Studio test, when the user creates a valid schedule, then one typed Paused schedule is persisted without a catalog check and can be managed by terminal/API and Studio UI.

Given a paused schedule or a concurrent editor, when explicit Resume acknowledges the current confirmed revision or an update uses a stale version, then activation is fully validated or returns a defined conflict without unintended enabling; retry cannot duplicate a schedule. Every successful Resume, including empty uncertainty acknowledgment, atomically records an immutable activation event.

Given aligned cron and an explicit timezone, when preview and dispatcher resolve the same reference time, then next UTC/local/offset occurrences match, skip DST gaps and choose only the first fallback slot; invalid grammar/zone/nonzero seconds are rejected.

Given a due unready or forbidden test, when the worker decides the occurrence, then durable COMPILE_REQUIRED or the specific denial is visible without compile, confirmation, browser execution or fake video.

Given active and author-paused schedules, when affecting inputs change and are reconfirmed, then neither resumes implicitly; explicit Resume acknowledges the exact new revision while already accepted run snapshots remain unchanged. Metadata edits and failed optional unchanged-input recompiles do not falsely revoke readiness.

Given two workers and injected crashes across persistence boundaries, when they process the same nominal occurrence, then at most one accepted execution/ledger linkage exists and occurrence decision plus advancement are committed atomically or all roll back.

Given fallback DST, schedule-version change/removal recreation or years of missed slots, when recurrence is resolved, then stable local-slot uniqueness prevents repeat effects and missed work is summarized with bounded processing rather than replayed.

Given capacity or temporary pre-acceptance outage, when one nominal occurrence is retried within grace, then it retains identity/cursor and creates at most one run; after expiry it is settled visibly and future recurrence advances without catch-up. Pause/update/removal and affecting invalidation settle an outstanding deferred slot atomically with explicit lifecycle reason and no send; Resume never revives it. Capability-off history shows disabled/expired truthfully; on reenable expired deferred identity settles GRACE_EXPIRED without send before future advancement, while within-grace identity can be accepted once.

Given acceptance racing pause/remove/delete or a global disable, when transactions settle, then only serialized eligible acceptance occurs; pause/remove preserve accepted work while test lifecycle/global disable retains existing dispatcher denial and explicit cancel behavior.

Given accepted/refused/legacy occurrences and expired evidence, when authorized operators read paginated history/details, then actual scheduled provenance and run links are honest, legacy source is Unknown, and unavailable video never rewrites execution outcome. Clean Resume creates immutable human actor/time provenance and occurrences retain that activation after later actors edit, Resume or recreate the schedule. Run GET/list/SSE and withTestName preserve activationId/activatedBy/activatedAt from the accepted occurrence event; manual/legacy activation metadata remains null.

Given missing production authorization wiring or grant/secret permission revoked before acceptance or send, when schedule work attempts execution, then it fails closed; no token/secret value is stored or logged and local fixtures are not production approval.

Given MSW-backed editor/list flows and network/readiness/version errors, when keyboard-only users create/view/edit/pause/resume/remove, then labelled controls retain input, state explanations/preview are truthful and focus/status announcements work without implicit authoring actions.

Given a non-DONE manual or scheduled ledger row for the test, when a due scheduled occurrence is considered, then it is skipped for overlap without locking that ledger row or modifying existing manual-run permission.

Given terminal DISPATCH_UNKNOWN, START_TIMEOUT or STALE relevant to the test, when future recurrence is considered, then it remains durably blocked until investigation plus audited uncertainty acknowledgment and Resume; only future slots can execute.

nonFunctional.description: Bound due selection/processing and preserve ordinary REST/check responsiveness; scheduled and manual executions share existing global/per-CSI active quotas and runner admission.
nonFunctional.metric: No quota overrun; bounded batch and per-CSI attempts; representative load evidence required before production.

nonFunctional.description: One occurrence cannot accept duplicate browser executions across replica races or crash/restart; no ambiguous execution is automatically replayed.
nonFunctional.metric: At most one durable accepted ledger link per occurrence/local slot; crash-boundary integration cases.

nonFunctional.description: Use injected clocks and deterministic shared recurrence with bounded iteration, including DST, irregular cron and long outage boundaries.
nonFunctional.metric: Preview/due parity and bounded long-gap test cases pass; no unbounded slot loop.

nonFunctional.description: Current execution and separate secret-use permissions fail closed; immutable source/evidence protection and transient secret handling remain.
nonFunctional.metric: Authorization denial at activation/acceptance/send; no resolved secret/token persistence or log leakage.

nonFunctional.description: Paginated bounded schedule history, keyboard-operable accessible management and responsive summaries preserve current Studio list patterns.
nonFunctional.metric: Meaningful MSW/Playwright keyboard/focus/error and pagination scenarios pass.

nonFunctional.description: Rotate bounded due selection across CSIs, skipping saturated/deferred targets within the pass; retain bounded-cardinality metrics and no guaranteed browser-start SLA by assumption.
nonFunctional.metric: Saturated-CSI integration scenario permits other eligible CSI work; metrics do not label each UUID.

nonFunctional.description: Deploy additive forward-only migrations, preserve legacy inert scheduling metadata and immutable audit/dedup anchors independently of history/video retention.
nonFunctional.metric: Fresh/upgrade migration and retention/recreation duplicate tests pass; no unintended activation.

nonFunctional.description: Production scheduling is default off and cannot activate with provisional/local principal authorization; accepted-run recovery/cancellation remain operable when due producer is disabled.
nonFunctional.metric: Unwired production denies authorization; profile/feature-flag tests and rollback rehearsal demonstrate no new scheduled acceptance.

constraints.description: Existing generic schedules require a check ID; use typed Studio schedules/occurrences and reuse existing worker/ShedLock plus Studio acceptance/ledger/dispatcher. Do not create dummy checks or introduce Quartz/another queue.
constraints.impact: Preserve distinct schedule target and execution contracts.

constraints.description: Use current Java 21/Spring/PostgreSQL and frontend React/TypeScript/MUI dependencies and centralized API client; do not upgrade stack as part of scheduling.
constraints.impact: Research verifies current manifests instead of trusting historic prose.

constraints.description: Use one-test-per-transaction test -> schedule -> existing occurrence -> global quota -> CSI quota lock order, with nonlocking overlap ledger reads; preserve callbacks and manual admission idempotency.
constraints.impact: Prevents lock inversion and regression of manual execution.

constraints.description: Use DB-enforced scheduled occurrence identity: unique nullable ledger occurrence FK, with scheduled manual key/digest null; history partition locator is soft and accepted linkage targets durable ledger.
constraints.impact: Public arbitrary manual keys cannot collide via prefixes; retention is compatible.

constraints.description: Exclude suites, bulk/multiple schedules, environment matrices, unified catalog/dashboard/report projections, notifications/remediation, implicit compile/confirmation and automatic ambiguous browser retry.
constraints.impact: Bound authorized MVP to individual saved-test scheduling.

constraints.description: Established real on-demand trust and approved live background identity/vault grants are release gates; no per-test prior-PASS admission guard is added.
constraints.impact: Local fail-closed implementation/demos can complete without claiming production readiness.

constraints.description: Preserve dirty pre-existing code, existing manual permissions, pagination/deep links/evidence semantics and inert legacy schedule string; no automatic migration to enabled schedules.
constraints.impact: Implementation diffs must be attributable to scheduling and backward compatible.

constraints.description: Mock-first frontend consumes matching typed Studio/OpenAPI/MSW contracts; operational schedule functions must remain API/terminal-usable independently of UI.
constraints.impact: Independent frontend work must not bypass readiness/production gates.

assumptions.description: Working defaults: individual test, one schedule, create paused then explicit Resume, current confirmed activation revision, zero-second minute cron, UTC fallback, fixed 60-second minimum in this increment and configurable grace defaulting to 300 seconds.
assumptions.status: Adopted working engineering defaults by root; user may steer; production sizing not approved.

assumptions.description: Production chooses an approved CSI/environment service principal unless PUT Core requires renewable human delegation; local deterministic grants never enable production.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Identity adapter contract must change; production remains blocked.

assumptions.description: Typed standalone Studio tables and durable ledger linkage are accepted integration direction; exact linkage constraints and retention will be finalized in architect research.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Migration/admission sequencing must change before implementation.
assumptions.status: Technical choices closed by implementation-contract.md and research.json, subject independent critique.

assumptions.description: No numerical throughput, browser-start SLA, delivery date or retention period is promised; capacity and retention configuration require pilot operations review.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Operational configuration and acceptance envelope require explicit change.

domainModel.description: Test with immutable CSI, saved configuration and confirmed executable revision.
Stable per-test schedule/tombstone with cron/zone, author intent, effective blocked state, version, activation revision/principal and independent nominal due/poll cursor.
Durable nominal UTC and local slot identity with immutable target/activation attribution, decision and optional accepted execution.
relationships: has_one nullable linked durable ledger execution

domainModel.description: Existing globally identified accepted work owns dispatch/recovery and scheduled FK identity; partitioned execution history/evidence are linked separately.
Approved service-principal/delegation reference with current CSI/environment execution and separate secret entitlement, never copied login JWT.
Immutable event created on every successful Resume with server-derived human actor/time, schedule version, owned test/CSI/confirmed revision and environment/principal snapshots.

interactions.description: Saved test editor or row menu opens schedule form; authoritative preview; create Paused; explicit Resume acknowledges revision/principal and next future due.
Save changes through existing authoring; schedule intent persists but effective dispatch blocks; prepare/review/confirm; explicit Resume is required.
Pause or remove stops future acceptance, preserves accepted work/audit, offers actual run links for accepted occurrences and reason-only rows for refusals.

edgeCases.scenario: Two replicas or crash after partial persistence
edgeCases.handling: Atomic transaction/DB occurrence identity resolves one accepted execution or rollback; recover from durable ledger.
Test-first locking and exact activation revision reject changed inputs; no implicit Resume or altered accepted snapshot.
Shared earlier-offset resolver and stable version-independent local-slot dedup prevent repeat effects.

edgeCases.scenario: Long downtime, capacity or temporary authorization lookup outage
edgeCases.handling: Bounded missed-range audit and latest eligible within grace; defer same pre-acceptance occurrence or deny fail-closed; settle expiry visibly.

edgeCases.scenario: Manual run closes with uncertain outcome
edgeCases.handling: DISPATCH_UNKNOWN, START_TIMEOUT or STALE durably blocks until investigated/audited exact uncertainty acknowledgment and future-only Resume.

edgeCases.scenario: Forbidden management, revoked background/secret grant or missing production integration
edgeCases.handling: Non-disclosing reads and current fail-closed authorization; no scheduled runner send.

edgeCases.scenario: Pause/remove/global disable races accepted browser work
edgeCases.handling: Serialize future acceptance; preserve accepted snapshot/recovery and existing queued-vs-admitted lifecycle; cancel explicitly.

edgeCases.scenario: Legacy inert JSON or expired partitioned execution/evidence
edgeCases.handling: Never autoactivate; source Unknown and honest expired link behavior; preserve durable duplicate/audit anchors.

edgeCases.scenario: Deferred slot superseded by lifecycle mutation
edgeCases.handling: Under test/schedule/occurrence locks settle without execution as SKIPPED/SCHEDULE_PAUSED, SCHEDULE_UPDATED or SCHEDULE_REMOVED; affecting test/revision/lifecycle invalidation uses REFUSED existing specific code; retain nominal/grace/activation audit.

terminology.definition: Nominal recurring slot instant, distinct from acceptance and browser start.
Explicit authorization acknowledging confirmed revision, grant and any investigated uncertainty for future unattended recurrence.
Durable scheduled-slot decision; may exist without an accepted browser execution.
Enabled or paused choice preserved independently of readiness/authorization effective block.
Timezone and local scheduled date/time without offset; duplicate protection spans schedule versions and repeated DST offsets.
Same not-yet-accepted occurrence waits within bounded grace; it is not a new execution retry.
